text:
Juraj Slafkovsky scored 30 goals last season and put up 8 points in 6 games for Slovakia at the Olympics. This season he has 2 goals in 21 games, and none in his last twelve.

Our numbers read this as a slump, not a decline. He has 7.7 expected goals (the quality of his chances) and is shooting 4%, against a usual range of about 11 to 16. Over his last ten games he generated 4.0 expected goals on his own shots, more than his usual 3.8, yet scored nothing. That is the definition of due: he keeps getting the looks, and goals tend to follow chances. Only 2 of his 13 points are goals; Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking calls him a setup man (8.9 primary shot assists per 60 last season).

The concern is at the other end. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.17 more expected goals per 60 with him on the ice last season, bottom 7% of forwards, and this season Montreal's five-on-five share of expected goals is 4.0 points worse with him than without.

The first overall pick of 2022 is 22. Watch the defensive numbers as closely as the goals.
